claims.claim_vi: The source describes four retry strategies: linear backoff (simple, may cause retry storms under high concurrency), linear jitter backoff (randomness spreads retries but a linear base may still synchronise), exponential backoff (reduces load, may delay resolution when a quick retry would help), exponential jitter backoff (additive or multiplicative jitter, fewer collisions, sometimes longer than necessary delays).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Toy run: 1000 clients all fail at tick 0, the server accepts 100 requests per tick, 8 retries, base 2, cap 64. Without jitter (linear or exponential) 100 clients give up after 5400 requests, largest retry wave 900, finishing at tick 72 / 254; with additive jitter all 1000 succeed after 2560 requests, largest wave 326, finishing at tick 22 / 26; exponential full jitter 3128 requests, largest wave 574, tick 23.
claims.verified_by: Run by the author on 2026-10-19 with a small Python program (seed 1); counts of requests and ticks only.

design_notes_vi: Một khung bốn thẻ cho bốn cách chờ và một khung ghi chú kết quả mô phỏng.
source_deviations: The source describes four strategies qualitatively; the lesson keeps the four and adds a simulation with numbers that the source does not contain.
The simulation uses one fixed-capacity server and a synchronous start; it is a model, not a measurement of any real system.
The lesson separates when to retry (a different lesson) from how long to wait (this lesson).
